title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 131 (Revocation of continuing guarantee by surety's death)

content.overview: Section 131 provides that, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, the death of the surety operates as revocation of a continuing guarantee so far as future transactions are concerned. The rule is prospective and is subject to contrary contractual terms. It should not be read as automatically extinguishing liability already attached to transactions covered before the death.

sections.heading: Death of surety
sections.body: The death of the surety operates as revocation of a continuing guarantee, in the absence of a contract to the contrary.

sections.heading: Future transactions only
sections.body: Section 131 expressly limits the effect to future transactions. Identify the date of death and distinguish transactions already covered before death from later transactions.

sections.heading: Contractual qualification
sections.body: The words 'in the absence of any contract to the contrary' are material. Read the guarantee for any provision that changes the statutory default before concluding that the guarantee is revoked on death.

sections.heading: Relationship with Section 130
sections.body: Section 130 addresses revocation by notice to the creditor; Section 131 addresses the effect of the surety's death. Apply the trigger and timing in the relevant section.

examples.title: Recurring supply after death
examples.body: A guarantees payment for a series of credit supplies to B. A dies. Unless the contract provides otherwise, Section 131 treats the guarantee as revoked for future transactions; prior transactions must be analysed separately.

examples.title: Pre-death debt remains a separate question
examples.body: A surety dies after a covered supply has already been made but before payment falls due. Section 131's future-transaction wording does not itself decide every question about liability already attached; examine the guarantee and governing law.

hypotheticals.question: A surety dies while a continuing guarantee covers recurring future supplies. What is the statutory default?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under Section 131, absent a contract to the contrary, death revokes the continuing guarantee as to future transactions. Identify the date of death and any contrary contractual term.

hypotheticals.question: A covered transaction occurred before the surety's death, but payment is demanded afterwards. Does Section 131 automatically erase that liability?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 131 addresses revocation as regards future transactions. It does not itself say that liability already attached to a pre-death transaction is extinguished. Analyse the guarantee and applicable law for that existing liability.

hypotheticals.question: The guarantee expressly states that it continues notwithstanding the surety's death. What must be checked?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 131 contains the qualification 'in the absence of any contract to the contrary'. Interpret the clause carefully and assess enforceability and effect under the applicable law rather than ignoring the contractual qualification.

content.glance: Unless the contract provides otherwise, the surety's death revokes a continuing guarantee for future transactions; analyse pre-death transactions separately.
content.study:
## Statutory rule
Section 131 states that the death of the surety operates, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, as revocation of a continuing guarantee so far as regards future transactions.

## Apply the rule
1. Establish that the undertaking is a continuing guarantee within Section 129.
2. Identify the surety and establish the date of death.
3. Read the guarantee for any contract term to the contrary, because Section 131 expressly preserves that qualification.
4. Separate transactions already covered before death from future transactions after death.
5. Apply the statutory effect only to the future-transaction scope described in Section 131; do not assume the death automatically releases the estate from liabilities already attached or rewrites the underlying guarantee.

## Example
A guarantees a customer's recurring credit purchases from a supplier. The surety dies. Unless the guarantee contract provides otherwise, Section 131 treats the continuing guarantee as revoked for future transactions after death. The supplier must separately assess transactions and liabilities already covered before death under the guarantee's terms and applicable law.

## Relationship with Section 130
Section 130 deals with revocation by notice to the creditor; Section 131 deals with revocation by death, subject to a contract to the contrary. Both concern future transactions, but the triggering event differs.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: The death-based revocation rule is prospective as to future transactions and applies only in the absence of a contract to the contrary.

Check the guarantee for a contract to the contrary

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 131 provides that the death of a surety revokes a continuing guarantee, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, so far as future transactions are concerned. The key steps are to establish a continuing guarantee, identify the date of death, examine the contract's terms and distinguish future transactions from those already covered before death. Section 131 does not by itself settle every issue about liabilities already attached to pre-death transactions. Section 130 separately addresses revocation by notice to the creditor.
examples: A continuing guarantee for recurring future supplies is, absent contrary contract, revoked for future transactions when the surety dies.
A debt arising from a transaction already covered before death must be analysed separately; Section 131's future-transaction rule does not itself erase it.
distinctions: Section 131 is triggered by death of the surety; Section 130 is triggered by notice from the surety to the creditor.
Section 131 expressly preserves a contract to the contrary.
Revocation as to future transactions is different from extinguishing liability already attached to earlier transactions.
problemApplication: Confirm the guarantee is continuing under Section 129.
Read the contract for any term to the contrary.
Classify the transactions by whether they were covered before or arise after death.
State the prospective effect and separately analyse existing liabilities.
keyTakeaways: Section 131 concerns death of the surety under a continuing guarantee.
The default applies only in the absence of a contract to the contrary.
The effect is as to future transactions; existing covered liabilities require separate analysis.
Section 130 addresses notice-based revocation, a different trigger.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-131
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.myth: s-131 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.
